rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the laden ship as loaded with people and animals.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: يعني الموقر من الناس والدواب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr says the ship stalled mid-sea; Jonah confessed a grave sin and proposed a lot, which fell against him, so they cast him overboard.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جير: ركب يونس السفينة في البحر حتى إذا توسطت بهم ركدت

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Jonah identified himself as the fugitive servant preventing the ship from moving; the lot selected him, and he threw himself into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: لما احتبست السفينة قال: هاهنا عبد أبق من سيده، وهذا رسم السفينة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes explain sāhama as drawing lots.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: {فساهم}: فقارع (¬6). قال المبرد: وإنما أخذ من السهام

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives the word from the arrows used to draw lots.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: وإنما أخذ من السهام التي تحال للقرعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes take al-mudḥaḍīn to mean the defeated, whose lot was overruled.
rows.anchor: ققال ابن عباس (¬3) والمفسرون

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba relates the term to a proof being removed and to slipping, its root sense.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة. (يقال: أدحض الله حجته فدحضت، أي: أزالها فزالت)

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr says a whale waited open-mouthed for its Lord's command and took Jonah when he was cast from the ship.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لما استهموا في السفينة جاء حوت إلى السفينة فاغرا فاه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that God told the whale to take Jonah without tearing flesh or breaking bone; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes gloss the whale's taking him as gulping and swallowing, from the verb for swallowing a morsel.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون في قوله: {فالتقمه الحوت}: التهمه وابتلعه (¬8). يقال لقمت اللقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains alāma as doing something for which one is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: يقال: ألام إذا أتى ما يلام عليه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the description as Jonah's surrendering himself to his Lord.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني استلام إلى ربه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the word as blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يقول مذموم

rows.speaker: قتادة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qatada, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses it as having acted badly.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة عن ابن عباس: مسيء

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي خالد
rows.claim: Ismail b. Abi Khalid glosses the word as sinful.
rows.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: مذنب

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning say Jonah left before God's command and committed a sin that warranted corrective discipline to keep him on the path of refinement.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: كان يونس قد خرج قبل أن يأمره الله، وكان أذنب ذنبا استحق به التأديب

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid says Jonah's frequent prayer and remembrance in ease spared him from remaining in the whale as punishment until resurrection; al-Kalbi agrees.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: فلولا أنه كان في الرخاء قبل أن يلتقمه الحوت، {من المسبحين} يعني المصلين

rows.speaker: أبو زيد عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Zayd reports Ibn Abbas's explanation that the glorifiers are those who pray.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو زيد عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من المسبحين} من المصلين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Jonah used to pray frequently in times of ease.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان يكثر الصلاة في الرخاء

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi b. Anas says that without Jonah's righteous deeds he would have remained in the whale.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كان خلاله عمل صالح للبث في بطنه

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak b. Qays urges remembrance in ease so God remembers one in hardship, contrasting Jonah with Pharaoh, who remembered only while drowning and was rebuked.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك بن قيس (¬3) (¬4): اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة، فإن يونس كان عبدا صالحا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a righteous deed raises its doer, so whenever the person stumbles, he finds support.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في الحكمة: إن العمل الصالح يرفع صاحبه كلما عثر وجد متكئا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي عن أبي مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddi, reporting from Abu Malik, say Jonah stayed in the whale forty days; al-Kalbi gives the same duration.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج والسدي عن أبي مالك: لبث يونس في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil b. Hayyan says Jonah stayed in the whale three days.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says Jonah stayed in the whale seven days.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: سبعة أيام

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah stayed in the whale twenty days.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: عشرين يوما

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas's alternative view that Jonah glorified God while inside the whale.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من المسبحين} قال: يريد في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr identifies Jonah's glorification as his prayer, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers,” spoken in the whale, unlike the view that he prayed beforehand.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: يعني قوله: {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين} [الأنبياء: 87]

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah did not pray inside the whale but had already done good; he remained only a short time and was expelled well after being swallowed.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: ما كانت له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that angels heard Jonah's faint glorification, recalled his past good deeds, interceded, and God ordered the whale to cast him onto shore.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains al-arāʾ as an empty, open place.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله: {فنبذناه بالعراء} (¬1). يعني العراء: المكان الخالي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's people would acknowledge that the Mighty, Knowing God created the heavens and earth, affirming His justice and knowledge of creation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ولئن سألت قومك يا محمد (¬2) {من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم}

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi calls this confession a form of faith, though they contradict it by worshiping idols alongside God.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: وهذا إيمان منهم وهم يخالفون فيشركون به الأصنام

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning call this the height of ignorance: they acknowledge God as creator, then associate others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: هذا إخبار عن غاية جهلهم، إذ أقروا بالله خالق السموات والأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing the report of their answer, God begins describing Himself in the following verse.
rows.anchor: وقد تم الإخبار عنهم (¬5) ثم ابتدأ جل وعز دالا على نفسه فقال:

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the speech shifts from the unbelievers' reported answer to God's own description; otherwise they would say “for us,” not “for you.” The two attributes still describe the same God.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب # النظم: أخبر الله عما يقول الكفار إذا سئلوا عمن خلق السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land-making clause adds a true attribute to the attribute quoted from the unbelievers; its explanation was given at Ṭā Hā 20:53.
rows.anchor: صفة من صفاته أضافها -عز وجل- إلى الصفة التي حكاها عن الكفار؛ لأنها حق

rows.speaker: الحسن ومقاتل
rows.claim: Hasan and Muqatil take the guidance as finding one's destination while travelling.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: تهتدون في أسفاركم إلى مقاصدكم، وهذا قول الحسن ومقاتل،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas understands the guidance as reaching the truth by reflecting on the land God provided.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas contrasts measured rain for people's and animals' livelihood with the unmeasured flood sent to Noah's people, which drowned and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد # ليس كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر حتى أغرقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairs encompass all kinds, varieties, and colors, including male and female.
rows.anchor: أي الأصناف والضروب والألوان والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the masculine pronoun agrees with mā, the relative pronoun “what.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: التذكير ل: ما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says “backs” is plural though it refers to a singular word with collective meaning, like army or troop.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: أضاف الظهور إلى واحد فيه معنى الجمع بمنزلة الجيش والجند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing to recall is God's subjection of vehicles for travel on land and sea.
rows.anchor: يعني النعمة بتسخير ذلك لكم، مراكب في البر والبحر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the recollection as thanking God for providing the mount and carrying the rider on it.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو أن تقول: الحمد لله الذي رزقني هذا وحملني عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the recalled blessing as God's honoring people through these conveyances, supported by the statement that the children of Adam were honored and carried on land and sea.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس: تذكروا كرامة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the formula as saying God made the conveyance compliant and available.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ذلل لنا هذا المركب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the ship-riding formula is taught in 11:41, while this verse teaches the formula for riding camels.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قد علمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم الفلك بقوله: {بسم الله مجراها ومرساها}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people could not manage camels, ships, or the sea without God's subjection of them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: ولا طاقة لنا بالإبل ولا بالفلك ولا بالبحر لولا أن الله سخره لنا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes take muqrinīn to mean able or capable; Abu Ubayda glosses it as able to control something and cites a line about mastering difficult things.
rows.anchor: ومعنى المقرن: المطيق في قول المفسرين (¬3)، قال أبو عبيدة: فلان مقرن لفلان، أي: ضابط له

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth derives the word from being able to handle a horse or camel; al-Zajjaj and Ibn Qutayba give similar explanations, with Ibn Qutayba likening it to an equal in strength.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: أقرنت لهذا البرذون والبعير، أي قد أطقته، وكان اشتقاقه من قولك: صوت له قرنا مطيقا

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the statement looks declarative but functions as a command: if it were only a report, all people would act on it; compare 51:56, meaning God created them to be commanded to worship.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: هذا كله خبر عن ظاهره، ومعناه في الباطن أمر؛ لأنه لو كان خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says that earlier peoples gave the same reply as the people just discussed.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن غيرهم قالوا هذا القول فقال: {وكذلك} أي وكما قالوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the prosperous leaders as a town's kings, elite, and tyrants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: ملوكها وأشرافها وجابرتها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says “guided” or “following” can predicate the statement “we are,” with “on their tracks” attached to it, yielding “we follow their path.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق قوله: {مهتدون} و {مقتدون}، يصلح أن يكون جوابا ل: {إنا}، و {على} من صلته

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abu Ishaq parses “on their tracks” as one predicate of “we are,” with “guided” and “following” as further predicates.
rows.anchor: ويصلح أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر، فيكون (على آثارهم) خبر (إنا) ومهتدون [خبرا ثان]

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they will be asked whether they gave thanks for the honor bestowed on them.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: أي عن هذا الشرف هل أديتم شكره

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil takes the question as a rebuke to those who rejected the Quran: why did you reject it?
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني من كذب به، كأن يسأل: لم كذب به؟ (¬2) فيسأل سؤال توبيخ.

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says they will be asked to give thanks for the honor God gave them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: سوف تسألون عن شكر ما جعله الله لكم من الشرف

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another view says they will be questioned about the Quran, their obedience to its commands, and their duty to uphold its rights.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: تسألون عن القرآن وعملكم بما أمرتم به فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Malik as the keeper of Hell.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد خازن جهنم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the damned ask Malik to have God end their lives; Malik remains silent for forty years.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: ليقض علينا الموت

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the plea as asking God to bring death so they can rest from the torment.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لينزل علينا ربك الموت، والمعنى أنهم توسلوا بمالك إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Malik does not answer them for a thousand years.
rows.anchor: وألف سنة فيما روي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says Malik stays silent for eighty years, each day equal to a thousand years by their reckoning, then tells them they will remain.
rows.anchor: قال القرظي: لا يجيبهم ثمانين سنة، كل يوم منها كألف سنة مما تعدون

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses the answer as meaning that they remain in the torment.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول مقيمون في العذاب

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning call “tasting” death metaphorical: it is enduring the pains and causes that bring death, while death itself is an accident that cannot literally be tasted.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: جعل الموت في مقاساة الآلام والأسباب التي يحدث عندها الموت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of no death heightens the joy of Paradise's pleasant life; in Hell, repeated death from suffering is withheld, increasing anguish and distress.
rows.anchor: إن أهل الجنة في حياة هنيئة بشارتهم بالخلود تزيدهم سرورا وقرة عين، وأهل النار يموتون موتات كثيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the excepted first death as the death experienced in this world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: التي كانت في الدنيا (¬5)، وقال مقاتل: يعني: المرة الأولى التي كانت في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reads illā as “other than”: they experience no death in Paradise beyond the first death they had in the world, paralleling 4:22.
rows.anchor: الموت البتة سوى الموتة الأولى التي ذاقوها في الدنيا، وهذا كما قال (¬7)

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra compares the exception to an expression where illā adds to what came before rather than subtracting from it, as in this verse.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الفراء قال: ومثله في الكلام: لك عندي ألف إلا مالك عندي من قبل فلان،

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some scholars of meaning take illā to mean “after,” yielding “after the first death.”
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: (إلا) بمعنى: بعد، أي: بعد الموتة الأولى

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: Another view takes illā to mean “but”: they have tasted the first death, but no further death.
rows.anchor: وقيل (إلا) بمعنى: لكن، كأنه قيل: لكن الموتة الأولى (¬2)، وقد ذاقوها

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the worldly death can be excepted from their state in Paradise because the blessed encounter its comfort and see their dwellings and open gates at death, already connected to Paradise's causes.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن قتيبة وجها حسنا فقال: إنما استثنى الموتة الأولى وهي في الدنيا، من موت في الجنة؛

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God made the Quran easy on Muhammad's tongue.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني القرآن يقول هوناه على لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose was that people take heed and believe, though they did not believe.
rows.anchor: لكي يتعظوا فيؤمنوا به فلم يؤمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reads the command to wait as waiting for their punishment, while they await the Prophet's destruction.
rows.anchor: يقول الله لنبيه: {فارتقب} يعني: فانتظرهم (¬2) العذاب فإنهم {مرتقبون} منتظرون هلاكك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation has the Prophet await victory over them while they expect to defeat and overpower him.
rows.anchor: ويقال: فانتظر الفتح والنصر عليهم، إنهم ينتظرون غلبتك وقهرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the opening challenge is explained in the parallel passage at Fatir 35:40.
rows.anchor: {قل أرأيتم} وهي مفسرة في سورة فاطر [آية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks for an earlier scripture that proves the claimed legitimacy of worshiping idols.
rows.anchor: {ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا} أي: ائتوني بكتاب من قبل القرآن فيه برهان ما تدعون

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Farra, and al-Zajjaj explain athāra as a remnant; Ibn Qutayba specifies a remnant of knowledge from earlier people, and al-Hasan relates it to something stirred up and extracted.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: أي بقية، ويقال: ناقة ذات أثارة، أي بقية من شحم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also allows athāra to mean something transmitted from the books of earlier peoples, and treats the form as a verbal noun like generosity or bravery.
rows.anchor: وزاد الفراء فقال: ويقال أو شيء مأثور من كتب الأولين، قال: وأثارة على المصدر مثل: السماحة والشجاعة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives athāra the sense of a sign of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وزاد الزجاج فقال: (أثارة) معناها علامة من علم

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives athāra from transmitted knowledge, the source of the term āthār for reports; he also records a sense of something beautiful to the eye, like a full attractive camel.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: أثارة ما يؤثر من علم، كقولك: هذا حديث يؤثر عن فلان، ومن ثم سميت الأخبار الآثار

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi groups the lexical explanations into three: a remnant, a transmitted report, or a mark/sign; the second sense is illustrated by al-Aʿsha's line.
rows.anchor: وهو ينقسم إلى أقوال ثلاثة: الأول: البقية، واشتقاقه من: أثرث الشيء أثيره إثارة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes athāra as a remaining portion of knowledge.
rows.anchor: الأول: البقية، واشتقاقه من: أثرث الشيء أثيره إثارة، كأنها بقية تستخرج

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas's gloss: bring something you transmit from a prophet who preceded Muhammad.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس؛ قال: يريد أو شيء ترويه عن نبي كان قبل محمد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it means a report from prophets that God has a partner; he attributes this view to Mujahid, Ikrima, and al-Qurazi.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أو رواية من علم عن الأنبياء أن لله شريكا (¬5)، وقال: هذا قول مجاهد وعكرمة والقرظي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: In al-Kalbi's narration, athāra means a remnant of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية الكلبي: بقية من علم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains it as special knowledge, perhaps a remnant preserved among learned specialists.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا معنى قول قتادة: خاصة من العلم؛ لأن الخاصة من العلم بقية منه بقيت عند خواص العلماء

rows.speaker: السلمي والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Sulami and al-Hasan read athara with a different vocalization, supporting a sense of knowledge held exclusively by its possessor; al-Wahidi calls this a good interpretation.
rows.anchor: ويؤكد ما قلناه قراءة السلمي والحسن (أو أثرة من علم) (¬3)، والمعنى على هذا: ائتوني بعلم تنفردون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi glosses athara or athāra as exclusive privilege; saying someone has athara in something means that person has a special claim to it.
rows.anchor: ويقال لفلان: أثرة بكذا أو أثارة، أي اختصاص

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة عن ابن عباس والشعبي
rows.claim: Abu Salama reports from Ibn Abbas and al-Shaʿbi that athāra means knowledge of drawing lines in the earth, a divinatory practice of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سلمة (¬4) عن ابن عباس والشعبي أيضا عنه في قوله: {أو أثارة من علم} قال: هو علم الخط

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that a prophet used to draw lines; whoever's line matches his would know that prophet's knowledge, challenging the idolaters to produce such evidence.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أنه قال

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes describe the glorious Quran as noble before God and abundant in good; its meaning was discussed at Hud 11.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: الكريم على الله الكثير الخير. وذكرنا معنى المجيد

words: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the oath's response is 50:4, “We know what the earth diminishes of them.”
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في جواب القسم، فقال الأخفش: جوابه {قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض}

words: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads the oath as “By Q and the glorious Quran, We know what the earth diminishes of them,” with the response-lām omitted because the preceding wording substitutes for it; he compares 91:1 and 91:9.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويكون المعنى: ق والقرآن المجيد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the response is omitted and indicated by the question at 50:3: the oath means they will surely be resurrected, which they deny; al-Zajjaj also chooses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: جواب القسم محذوف يدل عليه قوله: {أإذا متنا}

rows.speaker: كثير من الناس
rows.claim: Many take “rather, they wonder” at 50:2 as the oath's response; al-Wahidi says he treated this at the opening of Sad and notes the similar opening structure.
rows.anchor: وذهب كثير من الناس إلى أن الجواب قوله: {بل عجبوا} (¬6). وقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains rajʿ as a return or reversal, citing the verb in 9:83.
rows.anchor: الرجع معناه الرد. قال الله تعالى: {فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم}

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq parses rizqan either as an implied cognate object, “We provided them provision,” or as a purpose object, “We brought forth these things for provision.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما: على معنى رزقناهم رزقا,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emergence from graves is like the creation of plants; God likewise brings the dead out, as in 7:57.
rows.anchor: أي من القبور. والمعنى: كما خلقنا هذه الأشياء نبعثكم كقوله: {كذلك نخرج الموتى}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says rain falls like men's seminal fluid and flesh and bones grow upon the dead.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ينزل من السماء مطر كنطف الرجال تنبت عليهم اللحوم والعظام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil compares people emerging from their graves through rain to plants emerging from earth through rain.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مقاتل: يخرجون من القبور بالماء، كما أخرجنا النبت من الأرض بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The carriers bearing a load are clouds carrying the heavy weight of water.
rows.anchor: يعني السحاب التي تحمل وقرا، أي ثقلا من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smoothly moving things are ships, gliding easily through the water.
rows.anchor: يعني السفن تجري ميسرة في الماء جريا سهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to turn away from the polytheists after delivering the warning; he is not blameworthy because he conveyed the message.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأعرض عن هؤلاء المشركين فقد بلغت وأنذرت، وهو قوله: {فما أنت بملوم}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet feared punishment would descend on his people; Muqatil and Qatada agree, and the Companions feared revelation had stopped and punishment was imminent before the command to remind came.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فحزن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- لما نزلت هذه الآية مخافة أن تنزل بقومه العذاب.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Prophet is commanded to turn from unbelievers and admonish the believers, since the reminder benefits those who believe.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: عظ بالقرآن من آمن من قومك، فإن الذكرى تنفعهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil instead takes the command as warning Mecca's unbelievers with the Quran; the reminder benefits those destined to believe, and al-Wahidi says this better fits the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مقاتل. يقول: عظ كفار مكة بوعيد القرآن، فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi rejects al-Farra's grammatical argument: “he” refers to Gabriel, and the wāw is circumstantial, not coordination; the verb istawā takes one subject, as in 28:14 and 20:5.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما قالا: الواو في {وهو} واو الحال لا العطف، والضمير لجبريل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a nominative predicate containing a pronoun for the subject, not an adverb attached to istawā; it therefore does not prove that an overt nominative may coordinate with an unreinforced nominative pronoun.
rows.anchor: ولكنه من استوى الذي هو يقتصر فيه على فاعل واحد، كقوله: {ولما بلغ أشده واستوى}

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas that the Prophet saw Gabriel in his true form at the highest horizon, with six hundred wings; al-Kalbi gives a similar report.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: رأى رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- جبريل وهو بالأفق الأعلى في صورته له ستمائة جناح

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil places the horizon toward the sunrise; al-Kalbi calls it the sunrise, which the exegetes generally identify as above the east.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل {وهو} يعني جبريل {بالأفق الأعلى} يعني من قبل المطلع

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Gabriel usually came in human form; at Muhammad's request he appeared twice in his angelic form, once at Hira filling the eastern-to-western horizon, where Muhammad fainted, and once in heaven at the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن جبريل كان يأتي رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في صورة الآدميين فسأله رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the afterlife and this world belong to God; no one owns or receives anything from either without His permission, refuting what the unbeliever wishes for.
rows.anchor: أي لا يملك فيهما ولا منهما أحد شيئا إلا بإذنه؛ لأنهما (¬2) له.
